note.explanation: Environmental problems can be reduced by lowering pollution at its source and protecting people from polluted air. Planting trees, using catalytic converters, removing sulphur dioxide from flue gas and switching to renewable energy are important strategies. When air quality is poor, people—especially high-risk groups—should reduce outdoor exposure and follow safety advice.
examples: A catalytic converter changes harmful carbon monoxide into carbon dioxide.
Solar and wind energy can generate electricity without burning fossil fuels.
note.checkAnswer: Planting trees, using catalytic converters, reducing sulphur dioxide from flue gas and using renewable energy can help reduce environmental issues.
note.simple: Make less pollution, use cleaner energy, and avoid breathing polluted air.
note.checkQuestion: Name one strategy that can reduce harmful emissions from automobiles.
note.title: Strategies to reduce environmental issues
steps: Plant trees: they absorb carbon dioxide during photosynthesis and trap some particulate matter on their surfaces.
Use catalytic converters: they change nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons into less harmful substances.
Reduce sulphur dioxide: use fuels with less sulphur or remove sulphur dioxide from flue gas using an adsorbent such as calcium oxide.
Use renewable resources such as sunlight, wind, water, geothermal energy and biomass.
When air quality is poor, limit outdoor activity, use a well-fitted N95 mask if going out, keep indoor air clean and seek medical advice for worrying symptoms.
note.answer: A catalytic converter reduces harmful emissions from an automobile engine by changing them into less harmful substances.

written.text: Q10.4. How can you reduce the emission of CO present in the gases emitted by the burning of fuel in the automobile engines?
written.finalAnswer: Use a catalytic converter in the automobile exhaust system; it oxidizes CO to CO₂.

rubric.why: Naming the method identifies the control strategy.
rubric.how: State that a catalytic converter is used in the automobile exhaust system.

rubric.why: Locating the converter in the exhaust system shows how it treats the emitted gases.
rubric.how: Place the converter in the automobile exhaust system.

rubric.why: The chemical change explains how the harmful emission is reduced.
rubric.how: State that the converter oxidizes carbon monoxide to carbon dioxide.

rubric.why: The final product must be identified correctly.
rubric.how: End with carbon dioxide as the product formed from CO.

modelAnswer: A catalytic converter is used in the exhaust system of an automobile.
It oxidizes CO to CO₂.
2CO(g) + O₂(g) → 2CO₂(g).
Thus, the emission of CO is reduced.

written.text: Q10.3. What is air quality index? What information does it convey?
written.finalAnswer: Air quality index (AQI) is a rating system that shows how bad the atmosphere is around you; it conveys the quality of the air and the level of health risk.

rubric.why: The definition begins by identifying what kind of measure AQI is.
rubric.description: Define AQI as a rating system.
rubric.how: Write that AQI is a rating system.

rubric.why: The rating is about the surrounding atmosphere or air.
rubric.how: Explain that it shows how bad the atmosphere or air is around a person.

rubric.why: The answer must state the information that the index provides.
rubric.how: Say that it indicates the quality of the air.

rubric.why: The section explains that health risk increases as AQI increases.
rubric.how: State that a higher AQI indicates greater health risk.

modelAnswer: Air quality index (AQI) is a rating system that shows how bad the atmosphere around you is.
An AQI under 50 is considered good in quality, while an AQI over 300 is considered hazardous.
As the AQI number increases, so does the risk to health.

written.text: Q10.4. Who are high risk groups and why is pollution more dangerous for them?
written.finalAnswer: High-risk groups include children under 18, adults over 65, people with chronic heart or lung disease, diabetic people and outdoor workers with prolonged exposure. Pollution is more dangerous for them because it can affect their lungs, heart and brain, enter their bloodstream and cause serious illness or premature death.

rubric.why: Correctly identifying the groups shows who is especially vulnerable.
rubric.how: Give examples such as children, older adults, people with chronic heart or lung disease, diabetic people or outdoor workers.

rubric.why: Stating affected body systems explains the danger of pollution.
rubric.how: Explain that polluted air may affect the lungs, heart and brain.

rubric.why: The section specifically explains that air pollutants can enter the bloodstream.
rubric.description: Explain how pollutants affect the body.
rubric.how: State that pollutants can enter the blood.

rubric.why: A serious health consequence completes the explanation.
rubric.how: Mention a consequence such as hospitalization, cancer, poor quality of life or premature death.

modelAnswer: High-risk groups include children under 18, adults over 65, people with chronic heart or lung disease and diabetic people.
Outdoor workers may also be at higher risk because of prolonged exposure.
Breathing polluted air may affect their lungs, heart and brain, and air pollutants can enter their bloodstream.
This may cause coughing, itchy eyes, poor quality of life, hospitalization, cancer or premature death.

written.text: Q10.5. Describe three strategies to address environmental issues.
written.finalAnswer: Three strategies are planting trees, using catalytic converters and reducing sulphur dioxide emissions; using renewable resources is another important strategy.

rubric.why: This is one strategy specifically discussed in the section.
rubric.how: Explain that trees absorb carbon dioxide and trap particulate matter.

rubric.why: This identifies a method for reducing harmful automobile emissions.
rubric.how: Explain that converters reduce nitrogen oxides and oxidize CO and hydrocarbons.

rubric.why: Reducing sulphur dioxide emissions is a separate strategy from the other methods.
rubric.how: Mention low-sulphur fuels or flue gas desulphurization using an adsorbent such as calcium oxide.

rubric.why: Using renewable energy helps discourage excessive use of fossil fuels.
rubric.description: Describe the use of renewable resources.
rubric.how: Give examples such as solar or wind energy.

rubric.why: The question specifically asks for three strategies.
rubric.description: Provide at least three distinct strategies.
rubric.how: Clearly identify three separate approaches.

modelAnswer: 1. Plant trees. During photosynthesis, plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen, and particulate matter deposits on their surfaces.
2. Use catalytic converters in automobile exhaust systems. They reduce nitrogen oxides and oxidize CO and hydrocarbons into less harmful products.
3. Reduce sulphur dioxide emissions by using fuels with less sulphur or by using flue gas desulphurization with adsorbents such as calcium oxide.
Using renewable resources such as solar and wind energy is also important because it reduces the excessive use of fossil fuels.

written.text: Q10.1. Major Pakistani cities experience a very high AQI in winter which renders them the most polluted cities in the world. Point out some of the major causes of high AQI in these cities.
written.finalAnswer: Major causes include emissions from vehicles, industries and coal-fired power plants that burn fossil fuels, along with smoke and particulate matter; winter conditions can also allow polluted air to build up.

rubric.why: Vehicle emissions are a major human source of air pollutants.
rubric.how: Mention emissions from automobiles or other vehicles.

rubric.why: Industrial emissions are another major pollution source.
rubric.how: Mention smoke or gases from industries and industrial machines.

rubric.why: Burning fossil fuels releases pollutant gases into the atmosphere.
rubric.how: Mention fossil-fuel burning, including coal-fired electricity plants.

rubric.why: Particulate matter and smoke contribute to poor air quality.
rubric.how: Include particulate matter, smoke or pollutant gases.

rubric.why: Explaining how winter conditions can worsen accumulation addresses the seasonal setting of the question.
rubric.description: Explain why pollution can accumulate in winter.
rubric.how: Note that winter weather and atmospheric conditions can prevent polluted air from dispersing easily.

modelAnswer: Vehicles, industries and coal-fired electricity-generating plants burn fossil fuels and release pollutant gases.
These emissions include smoke and particulate matter, which worsen the air quality index.
In winter, weather conditions can make it harder for polluted air to disperse, so pollutants build up over cities.

examTips: This section can be tested with short questions asking for a strategy, a definition or a use of renewable energy.
Constructed-response questions may ask how catalytic converters reduce CO or how solar energy is useful; name the method and explain the change or use.
For descriptive questions, organise the answer as numbered strategies and include a clear explanation of each one.
For AQI and high-risk-group questions, state what AQI indicates, mention the key thresholds given in the text and identify the groups at higher risk.
Chemical equations can earn marks: write the balanced equations for the catalytic converter reactions when the question asks how it works.

explain.title: Plants help remove air pollution
explain.body: Your textbook describes photosynthesis as the process in which plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. Particulate matter can also deposit on leaves, branches and trunks.

explain.title: Catalytic converters treat automobile exhaust
explain.body: A three-way catalytic converter reduces nitrogen oxides to nitrogen and oxygen, oxidizes carbon monoxide to carbon dioxide, and oxidizes hydrocarbons to carbon dioxide and water.

explain.title: Reduce sulphur dioxide and fossil-fuel use
explain.body: Sulphur dioxide emissions can be reduced by using fuels with less sulphur or by removing sulphur dioxide from flue gas. Calcium oxide is an example of an adsorbent used in flue gas desulphurization. Renewable energy sources can also reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

explain.title: Know the AQI and protect yourself
explain.body: AQI rates how bad the surrounding air is. An AQI under 50 is considered good, while a value over 300 is hazardous. When air quality is bad, reduce outdoor time, consider a well-fitted N95 mask if you must go out, keep indoor air clean and speak to a doctor about worrying symptoms.

mistakes: Do not say plants absorb oxygen and release carbon dioxide during photosynthesis; the section says they absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen.
Do not mix up the catalytic converter reactions: it oxidizes CO to CO₂ and reduces nitrogen oxides to nitrogen and oxygen.
Do not describe calcium oxide as a fuel; it is an adsorbent used to remove sulphur dioxide from flue gas.
Do not say that all masks filter fine particulate matter equally well; the section says well-fitted N95 masks have better filtration capabilities.
Do not write that a high AQI means good air quality; as AQI increases, so does the risk to health.
